D&C Orange No. 5 may be used in lipstick, mouthwash, and body lotion, with the following restrictions:

- In lipstick: Yes, up to 5.0 percent by weight of the finished product [2].  
- In mouthwash: Yes, for coloring mouthwashes as part of ingested cosmetics, in amounts consistent with current good manufacturing practice [6].  
- In body lotion (externally applied cosmetic): Yes, in amounts consistent with current good manufacturing practice [6].

21 CFR 70.3(v) defines "externally applied drugs and externally applied cosmetics" as those applied to external parts of the body and not to the lips or any body surface covered by mucous membrane. This definition supports that body lotions (as externally applied cosmetics) are included in the scope of use for D&C Orange No. 5 [7].

21 CFR 74.2255(a): The color additive D&C Orange No. 5 shall conform in identity and specifications to the requirements of § 74.1255 (a)(1) and (b). [1]  
21 CFR 74.2255(b): D&C Orange No. 5 may be safely used for coloring mouthwashes and dentifrices that are ingested cosmetics in amounts consistent with current good manufacturing practice. D&C Orange No. 5 may be safely used for coloring lipsticks and other cosmetics intended to be applied to the lips in amounts not exceeding 5.0 percent by weight of the finished cosmetic products. D&C Orange No. 5 may be safely used for coloring externally applied cosmetics in amounts consistent with current good manufacturing practice. [2]  
21 CFR 74.2255(c): The label of the color additive shall conform to the requirements of § 70.25 of this chapter. [3]  
21 CFR 74.2255(d): All batches of D&C Orange No. 5 shall be certified in accordance with regulations in part 80 of this chapter. [4]  
21 CFR 82.1255(a): The color additive D&C Orange No. 5 shall conform in identity and specifications to the requirements of § 74.1255(a)(1) and (b) of this chapter. D&C Orange No. 5 is restricted to the uses described in this section. [5]  
21 CFR 82.1255(b): The color additive D&C Orange No. 5 may be safely used for coloring externally applied drugs in amounts not exceeding 5 milligrams per daily dose of the drug. The color additive D&C Orange No. 5 may be safely used for coloring lipsticks and other cosmetics intended to be applied to the lips in amounts not exceeding 5.0 percent by weight of the finished cosmetic products, and for coloring mouthwashes, dentifrices, and externally applied cosmetics in amounts consistent with current good manufacturing practice. [6]  
21 CFR 82.1050: A batch of a straight color listed in this subpart may be certified, in accordance with the provisions of this part, for use only in drugs and cosmetics, if such batch conforms to the requirements of § 82.5 and to the specifications set forth in this subpart for such color. [8]
